706:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Bank means any financial institution chartered under the laws of any state or under the laws of the United States which is authorized to receive deposits in this state and which has a corporate structure authorizing the issuance of capital stock.
Depository financial institutions means a bank or a savings and loan association.
Gross receipts means gross receipts as defined in O.C.G.A. § 48-6-95.
Savings and loan association means any financial institution, other than a credit union, chartered under the laws of any state or under the laws of the United States which is authorized to receive deposits in this state and which has a mutual corporate form.
(Code 1991, § 13-116; Res. of 9-14-1983, § 1)
707:
In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93, there is hereby levied an annual business license tax upon all depository financial institutions located within the county at a rate of 0.25 percent of the gross receipts of such depository financial institutions.
(Code 1991, § 13-117; Res. of 9-14-1983, § 1)
708:
The minimum annual amount of business license tax due from any depository financial institution pursuant to this article shall be $1,000.00.
(Code 1991, § 13-118; Res. of 9-14-1983, § 2)
709:
Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93(c), each depository financial institution subject to this tax shall file a return of its gross receipts with the county tax commissioner on March 1 of the year following the year in which such gross receipts are measured. Such return shall be in the manner and in the form prescribed by the commissioner of the department of revenue based on the allocation method set forth in O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93(d). The county tax commissioner shall assess and collect the tax levied pursuant to this article based upon the information provided in such return.
(Code 1991, § 13-119; Res. of 9-14-1983, § 3)
710:
Taxes levied pursuant to this article shall be due no later than 30 days after filing of the return prescribed by section 28-126 unless extended by the board of commissioners.
(Code 1991, § 13-120; Res. of 9-14-1983, § 4)
711:
The director of community development is hereby directed to forward a copy of this article to each depository financial institution in the county and to the home office of each such depository financial institution if located outside the county.
(Code 1991, § 13-121; Res. of 9-14-1983, § 5)
State Law reference— Authorization to levy and collect a business license tax from depository financial institutions, O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93.
714:
In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 33-8-8.2, there is hereby levied for an annual tax upon each insurer doing insurance business within the unincorporated area of this county, in an amount equal to 2½ percent of the gross direct premiums received during the calendar year on all insurance, other than life insurance, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 33-3-5(2), (3), (4) and (5). The term "gross direct premiums" shall mean gross direct premiums as used in O.C.G.A. § 33-8-8.2(a).
(Code 1991, § 13-141; Res. of 1-1-1984, § 1)
715:
The county clerk is hereby directed to forward a duly certified copy of this article to the insurance commissioner within ten days of the enactment of the ordinance from which this section derives.
(Code 1991, § 13-142; Res. of 1-1-1984, § 2)
State Law reference— Taxation of insurance companies based on gross direct premiums received from insurance policies within the unincorporated areas of counties, Ga. Const., art. 9, § 4, ¶ 1(c); county tax on other than life insurance companies based on gross direct premiums, O.C.G.A. § 33-8-8.2.
718:
This article and the imposition of the county hotel/motel tax shall be levied throughout the county, including the areas within the various municipalities within the boundaries of the county.
(Code 1991, § 13-143; Ord. of 9-27-2005)
719:
The amount of the tax imposed pursuant to this article shall be at a rate of five percent pursuant to the authority of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(a)(3).
(Code 1991, § 13-144; Ord. of 9-27-2005)
720:
Any amounts collected pursuant to this article shall be expended in accordance with the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(a)(3).
(Code 1991, § 13-145; Ord. of 9-27-2005(2))
723:
In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 46-5-134.2, there is hereby imposed a prepaid wireless 911 charge as defined by O.C.G.A. § 46-5-134.2(a)(4) upon every prepaid wireless retail transaction occurring within the jurisdiction of the public service answering point in the amount of $0.75.
(Code 1991, § 13-146; Ord. No. 2011-04, 7-26-2011)
724:
Prepaid wireless 911 charges collected by sellers shall be remitted to the commissioner of the department of revenue at the times and in the manner provided by chapter 8 of title 48 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A. § 48-8-1 et seq.) with respect to the sales and use tax imposed on prepaid wireless calling service.
(Code 1991, § 13-147; Ord. No. 2011-04, 7-26-2011)
725:
The clerk of the county is hereby directed to file with the state revenue commissioner a certified copy of this article and amendments thereto, in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 46-5-134.2(j)(1), within ten days of enactment of this article.
(Code 1991, § 13-148; Ord. No. 2011-04, 7-26-2011)
726:
In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 46-5-134.2(j)(5), funds received by this county from charges imposed by this article shall be deposited in the emergency telephone system fund maintained by this county pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 46-5-134 and kept separate from general revenue of the jurisdiction; all such funds shall be used exclusively for the purposes authorized by O.C.G.A. § 46-5-134(f).
(Code 1991, § 13-149; Ord. No. 2011-04, 7-26-2011)
729:
As used in this article:
Applicant means a person applying for a permit for a broadband network project.
Permit means any local permit, license, certificate approval, registration, or similar form of approval required by policy, administrative rule, regulation, ordinance, or resolution with respect to a broadband network project.
(Ord. No. 2021-03, 8-24-2021)
730:
Meriwether County, Georgia shall appoint a single point of contact for all matters related to a broadband network project:
(1) The single point of contact documentation shall include;
Acting of Planning, Zoning, and Community Development Meriwether County, Georgia (706)672-1283 P.O. Box 370, Greenville, Georgia 30222
(2) The single point of contact shall be available for matters related to a broadband network project or may appoint a liaison who may direct such inquiry in real time, with general scope and responsibilities to include permitting and right-of-way.
(Ord. No. 2021-03, 8-24-2021)
731:
(a) Meriwether County shall determine whether an application or an amended application is incomplete and notify the applicant by email or by United States mail addressed to the primary address listed on the application of this determination by Meriwether County within ten calendar days of receiving an application.
(b) If Meriwether County does issue notification to the applicant on whether the application is incomplete, within ten calendar days, the application shall be assumed to be complete on the 11th day.
(Ord. No. 2021-03, 8-24-2021)
732:
(a) If Meriwether County determines that an application is not complete, a notification to the applicant by email or by United States mail addressed to the primary address listed on the application shall specify all required components of the submitted application that were considered "incomplete".
(b) Meriwether County's notification shall include a checklist of sequenced items that resulted in the application being deemed "incomplete" and the subsequent review timeline shall be as follows:
(1) The applicant has up to 40 calendar days from the date of notification of incompleteness to amend the application and make all necessary corrections; and
(2) If the applicant does amend the application within 40 calendar days, the application is deemed canceled.
(c) If, within ten calendar days after receipt of an amended application, Meriwether County does not respond to the applicant on whether the corrected application is incomplete, the amended application shall be assumed to be complete on the 11th day; and
(d) Meriwether County shall require a new submission and reset the application process and application fees, should an amended application be deemed incomplete.
(Ord. No. 2021-03, 8-24-2021)
733:
(a) If, on or before the 11th day as described in subsection 28-251(b) or subsection 28-252(c), an application is deemed complete, Meriwether County shall approve or deny an application within ten calendar days unless a joint meeting between the applicant and Meriwether County is deemed, as necessary.
(1) If a joint meeting is deemed necessary, the joint meeting must occur within 15 calendars days of notification of completion and the joint meeting shall include inquiry into, but not limited to, the following:
a. Where applicant is going to conduct work,
b. When the work will be conducted,
c. What type of work will be done,
d. Who Meriwether County can contact for specific details or related questions, and
e. Any permit seeking approval under application.
(b) The joint meeting may be continued by the applicant and Meriwether County for purposes of collecting additional information.
(c) Following conclusion of the joint meeting between the applicant and Meriwether County, Meriwether County shall deny or approve the application within ten calendar days.
(d) Upon final approval, any required permit permitted shall be deemed issued.
(Ord. No. 2021-03, 8-24-2021)
734:
(a) Any fee imposed by Meriwether County to review an application, issue a permit, or perform any other activity related to a broadband network project shall be reasonable, cost based, and nondiscriminatory to all applicants.
(b) Any application fee that exceeds $100.00 shall be considered unreasonable unless Meriwether County can provide documentation justifying such fee based on a specific cost.
(Ord. No. 2021-03, 8-24-2021)
735:
(a) Double fee. Meriwether County shall not require an application or permit(s) when already approved by an authorized state or federal jurisdiction. Provider shall notify and provide a copy of the approved permit to the single point of contact (or his liaison) prior to access of right-of-way within Meriwether County's jurisdiction.
(b) Application validity timeline. Any approved application shall be valid for six months from the date of approval. Should a provider not commence the service request qualified in the approved application within six months, the application shall expire, and Meriwether County shall require new permit approval and payment of any associated fees, as applicable.
(c) Single service drop. Meriwether County shall not require a permit for a broadband service provider to perform an installation of broadband service at an individual customer's service address as long as the facility being utilized only transverses a de minimis portion of the public right-of-way to reach the customer's property. The provider must still comply with the provisions of Chapter 9 of Title 25 of the O.C.G.A.
(Ord. No. 2021-03, 8-24-2021)
736:
Should any part of this article be found by a court of competent jurisdiction to be illegal, unenforceable, or void, the remaining parts of this article shall remain in full force and effect.
(Ord. No. 2021-03, 8-24-2021)
737:
(a) A Georgia Certified Broadband Ready Community has an affirmative duty to notify the Georgia Department of Community Affairs of any changes to the information submitted as part of its application; and
(b) Failure to notify Georgia Department of Community Affairs of changes may result in revocation of Meriwether County's Broadband Ready Certification or permit, should the certification or permit be granted.
(c) This article shall take effect immediately upon adoption by the governing body upon final reading.
